cards.explanation: The answer is True. Paul and his companions say it right to them: “This is how you already live, so you should do so all the more.” That's a compliment before the ask. Friends, I'd hang that one on my bakery wall.

The answer is to do it all the more. The ask is “This is how you already live, so you should do so all the more.” They're already doing well, and the letter says to keep climbing. Good bakers do the same thing with a batch they already love.

The answer is False. Paul and his companions don't say the instructions came on their own authority. The verse says, “For you know the instructions we gave you by the authority of the Lord Jesus.” These writers aren't making up rules on their own. They point to the Lord Jesus as the authority behind them, and that's a big deal, friends.
The answer is holy. The verse says, “For it is God’s will that you should be holy…” They don't have to guess. The letter tells them straight out, friends.
The answer is every one of the Thessalonians. The verse says, “…each of you must know how to control his own body in holiness and honor…” That's each of you, friends. Nobody is left out of this one.

The answer is the Gentiles who do not know God. The verse says, “…not in lustful passion like the Gentiles who do not know God…” The contrast is people who don't know God, and that's what the Thessalonians are told not to copy.

The answer is that the Lord will avenge all such acts. The verse says no one should violate or exploit his brother in this regard “…because the Lord will avenge all such acts…” It also says they'd been told and solemnly warned before. That's a serious one, friends, and I'm going to leave it right there.

The answer is False. The verse says the Lord will avenge all such acts, “…as we have already told you and solemnly warned you.” So Paul and his companions had warned them before. This letter is a reminder, not a first.
The answer is impurity. The verse says, “For God has not called us to impurity, but to holiness.” Notice the word us. The writers include themselves in that call, friends.

The answer is God Himself. The verse says, “Anyone, then, who rejects this command does not reject man but God, the very One who gives you His Holy Spirit.” So it's bigger than a letter from Paul. The command comes from God.

The answer is False. The verse says, “…you do not need anyone to write to you, because you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another.” So the reason they don't need a letter about it is that God had taught them. That's a good one to land on, friends.

The answer is that God Himself taught them. The verse says, “…you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another.” God was their teacher on this one, and you can't ask for a better one, friends.
The answer is Macedonia. The verse says, “And you are indeed showing this love to all the brothers throughout Macedonia.” That's a lot of ground covered, friends. Their love had some mileage on it.

The answer is to live quietly. It's one of the things listed: “…aspire to live quietly, to attend to your own matters, and to work with your own hands…” The word is aspire, which means it's something to reach for. Quiet is a goal, friends.

The answer is that they'll behave properly toward outsiders. The verse says, “Then you will behave properly toward outsiders…” Living quietly, minding their own matters and working with their own hands comes first. Then comes how they act toward people outside the church. Plain and simple, friends.
The answer is True. The verse ends, “…without being dependent on anyone.” That comes right after the quiet life, the own matters and the own hands. It's all one connected thought, friends.
